metaDescription: Acne treatment in Kalyani Nagar, Pune by an MD dermatologist: medical care, peels and procedures for teen and adult acne. Book a consultation.
intro: Acne is the most common reason patients walk into Skin Essence, and the most commonly mishandled. Most people reach a dermatologist in Pune after face washes, chemist creams, home remedies and salon facials. Some do nothing; steroid-containing fairness creams make acne worse and thin the skin.

Dr. Daksha Patel, an MD dermatologist with 17+ years of experience, begins with a proper assessment. Acne is not one condition: blackheads and whiteheads, red inflamed pimples, deep painful nodules and hormonal jawline acne in women each need a different approach. We examine your skin under magnification, ask about your cycle, diet, medicines and stress, and check for PCOS or other hormonal drivers where relevant.

Treatment usually combines prescription creams, oral medicines when needed, and in-clinic procedures that speed up clearing and lower the chance of scarring. Pune's humidity, commuting dust and hard water all play a part, so the routine you leave our Kalyani Nagar clinic with fits your actual day.
whoIsItFor: Teenagers with persistent blackheads, whiteheads or pimples that are not settling with over-the-counter products
Adults in their 20s to 40s with breakouts on the jawline, chin, chest or back, often linked to hormones
Anyone whose acne is leaving dark marks or pits, where early treatment prevents deeper scars
Patients whose acne flares before periods, with PCOS, or after stopping hormonal pills
People who have used steroid or 'fairness' creams and now have thin, sensitive, acne-prone skin

howItWorks.title: Assessment and grading
howItWorks.description: We grade your acne as mild, moderate or severe, identify the type of lesions and look for hormonal or lifestyle triggers. Every product you currently use is reviewed so we can stop anything that is harming your skin.

howItWorks.title: Medical plan
howItWorks.description: Prescription retinoids, benzoyl peroxide or antibiotics are chosen for your skin type. Moderate to severe acne may need oral antibiotics, hormonal therapy or isotretinoin, with blood tests where required.

howItWorks.title: Chemical peels and procedures
howItWorks.description: A course of peels chosen for your skin speeds up clearing: Black Peel for oily, inflamed acne, Jessner's peel for stubborn congestion, Azelac M for sensitive or pigment-prone skin, and Salipeel to unclog pores. Blackheads are extracted and painful cysts settled with an injection.

howItWorks.title: Review and maintenance
howItWorks.description: Follow-ups every 3 to 6 weeks let us adjust the plan. Once clear, a simple maintenance routine keeps acne away and we move on to marks or scars if needed.

sessionsAndDowntime.downtime: None for medical care; 1–3 days of mild peeling after a peel

aftercare: Use only the cleanser, moisturiser and sunscreen prescribed, and pause salon facials, scrubs and steam, which aggravate acne.
Do not squeeze or pick lesions. This is the main cause of dark marks and pitted scars.
Apply sunscreen every morning, even indoors. Sun exposure darkens post-acne marks.
Tell us before starting any supplement, protein powder or hormonal medicine; some worsen acne.

faqs.q: How long does acne treatment take to show results?
faqs.a: Most patients see a clear difference in 6 to 12 weeks. Creams act on lesions still forming under the skin, so the first weeks can look unchanged. Peels speed this up, but consistency at home matters most.

Not necessarily. Isotretinoin is reserved for severe, scarring or stubborn acne that has not responded to other treatment. If advised, Dr. Patel explains the dose, blood tests and precautions, including strict avoidance of pregnancy during and after the course.

faqs.q: Which chemical peel is right for my acne?
faqs.a: It depends on your skin. Black Peel, a black acetic acid peel, suits oily skin with inflamed pimples. Jessner's peel, a salicylic, lactic acid and resorcinol blend, tackles stubborn blackheads. Azelac M combines azelaic, mandelic and salicylic acids and is gentle on sensitive or pigment-prone skin. Salipeel, a salicylic acid peel, clears clogged pores.

faqs.q: Is my diet causing the acne?
faqs.a: High-glycaemic foods, whey protein supplements and, for some people, excess dairy can worsen acne. Diet alone rarely causes it, so we treat the skin medically and suggest specific changes rather than blanket restrictions.
Creams can cause mild dryness or stinging for two weeks. Peels feel like a warm tingle, and cyst injections are a quick pinprick.
